normal.name: Selena the Retro-Princess
normal.text: I randomly ran into the Saturn King of Fighters 95 ROM cart at a thrift store! It's a RAM expansion with game assets to speed up loading time - the game doesn't work without it, and of course it's region-locked to Japan and didn't get North American release. But the trick to getting it to work? Assuming you can launch a JP disk (ODE or region switch) you just wait until your North American BIOS screen "licensed by Sega" goes away, then connect the cart! Otherwise it'll give you an error. It's so funny that this works! #retrogaming #sega #saturn #kingoffighters
normal.media: 3 images: The KoF 95 ROM cart / The ROM cart in my North American Saturn (with Bluetooth controller dongle) / The Saturn KoF 95 title screen, showing the trick worked

normal.text: I really wish there were still single stick analogue joysticks that are NOT flightsticks. Something like the old Mach I and IIs. Really long throw that gives you pin accurate precision. normal.name: Raindrac
normal.text: I’m beginning to grow a fond appreciation for the GameCube now that I’m playing a lot of my old games on the Steam Deck. It’s just pure gaming! No gimmicks, dead servers or predatory micro-transactions. Everything just works. And it’s not as antiquated as games often are on older consoles, either, so it strikes a sweet spot that no other Nintendo console does. #gaming #retrogaming #gamecube #nintendo

normal.text: Now, for obvious reasons, I'd never condone warez. What I'm asking for is help with a legit CD copy that I own. With that said... I'm seeking info on manually creating a no CD crack for my copy of "The Incredible Machine: Even More Contraptions" game. I have a hex editor installed on my Win9X machine and I copied over all the files from the CD to the game install directory, but now I'm at the point of editing the EXE so it'll point to the files on the hard drive instead of asking for the CD. This is where I need help, hehe~ Any pointers would be appreciated! #retroGaming #retroComputing
